A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoQA and Fano-style accuracy-bound study. Their complete main text, equations, six figures, five tables and Appendices A.1–A.7 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B experiments on the authors' synthetic MHQA benchmark, including F1 results, ablations and fitted-parameter analyses (Section 5; Appendices A.6–A.7).

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablation results and empirical curve-fitting analyses in Section 5 and Appendices A.6–A.7.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same capacity-aware decomposition, dependency-explicit workflow and pruning/query-contraction procedure. Shortening the ablation description does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic noisy MHQA benchmark covering 1–4 hops and contexts from 0.5k to 10k tokens (Table 1; Appendix A.4). No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2 and 5: Direct, CoT, Self-Refine, Self-Consistency, ReAct, Plan-and-Solve and Self-Ask. The same ablation variants also remain in the Qwen3-14B comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain the Qwen3-8B/14B backbones, 300 samples per hop/context cell, F1 metric and decoding settings. Self-Consistency still uses five temperature-varied paths, Self-Refine uses one refinement iteration, and Appendix A.5 retains the same MAE grid-fitting protocol.

E4.justification: The decomposition/pruning ablations, hop/context robustness comparisons and qualitative error analysis are unchanged (Section 5.3; Table 2). Appendix A.7 retains the same Qwen3-8B analyses.

E5.justification: Both report point F1 and MAE values without across-run uncertainty intervals or significance tests. Appendix A.5 retains the same optional bootstrap suggestion; no new seed or repeated-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: Benchmark entries, fitted parameters, MAEs and plotted empirical points are unchanged (Tables 2–5; Figures 5–6). InfoQA's overall 2–4-hop F1 remains 0.86 for Qwen3-14B and 0.74 for Qwen3-8B.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its corollaries, the information-demand model and the error-accumulation equations are mathematically unchanged. Appendices A.2–A.3 retain identical definitions, assumptions, derivations and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same accuracy-cliff claim, dual MHQA challenges and positioning of InfoQA as a multi-call proof of concept. No substantive claim is strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: The capacity-overflow and error-accumulation interpretations remain unchanged, as do the explanations of semantic drift and failures under very long contexts (Section 5.3). Section 7 retains the same future-work and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, dataset-generation pseudocode and fitting details are unchanged (Section 5.1; Appendices A.4–A.5). The code/dataset link and reproduction-archive statement are also retained; the statement only moves pages.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. 'Wong et al., 2023' becomes 'Zamfirescu-Pereira et al., 2023', but both identify the same 'Why Johnny Can't Prompt' paper; this is an author-metadata update rather than a new citation.

P1.justification: Limited wording edits simplify Section 2.3 and the ablation paragraph, and 'Related Works' becomes 'Related Work'. Bibliographic author lists, capitalization and venue/DOI fields are revised, while the narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Text reflow shifts Figures 2–3 and Table 1 vertically and moves the ethics/reproducibility statements from page 11 to page 10. Figure graphics, captions, axes and table structures remain unchanged; early appendix proofs also reflow across pages.

improvement.justification: v3 provides small wording refinements and fuller bibliographic attribution while preserving all scientific content, experimental evidence and reproducibility information. The bibliography edits also introduce an inconsistent 'ICLR ’2025' abbreviation for Xu et al.'s computational-linguistics venue. These limited editorial gains and defects do not meaningfully change the paper's overall clarity, rigor or evidential support.
